direction.comments: The direction on a macroscale is grandly amazing as he builds this epic that transports you to Ancient Greece during the Homeric Iliad and Odyssey, using many practical sets and filming in similar regions to Greece to make everything feel 'real', executing the fight scenes very well to make this feel like an action-packed epic that transcends the genre, and building this vast world to show how far away Odysseus is from home and how far of a trip it is (both physically and mentally); the direction on a microscale is good, but does not match the macroscale as some of the interpersonal scenes feel a bit stiff (especially with the script and dialogue the actors have to work with), taking a step back from Oppenheimer as it feels like Christopher Nolan prioritized this movie on a grand scale that the microscale felt a bit like an afterthought; storytelling is very good as Nolan uses his traditional non-linear style to make an ancient literary classic like Homer's Odyssey feel like a Nolan Movie, starting the movie at the end and using flashbacks to show the journey; tension is built very well with multiple horror sequences like the Cyclops and Circe sequences making this the closest we're ever going to get to a horror Christopher Nolan movie, and while emotional tension is good as you do care for Odysseus and Penelope's struggles to reunite, it is not as strong as I would have liked it to be; tonally, this movie feels like a companion piece to Interstellar with its themes and world-building, trading Space for Ancient Greece (though it is not as strong)

performance.comments: Very much is Odysseus, playing a very stoic, hardened character; while it may not be Oscar-worthy, he really shows why he is a leading man and effortlessly carries the movie; brings out the best in his castmates with all the performances flowing through him to enable strong chemistry across the board

Very much a typical Tom Holland character, since this performance basically feels like his Spider-Man character, especially with the accent; has decent chemistry with the cast, with his dynamic with Jon Bernthal being stronger than with Anne Hathaway

Shows a good range of emotions, particularly as she is grieving and missing her husband; she helps carry the movie with her power and charisma despite some of her dialogue feeling muffled due to poor sound mixing; her chemistry is strong with Matt Damon, but decent with the rest of the cast
Plays a typical bad guy, following standard villain tropes without any real depth
Despite her high billing, she really is barely in this movie; does fine in the sequences she is in, but really isn't given that much material to rate off of

Creates a real menacing character as Circe in the 4 to 5 minutes of screen time she's in; she really brings out the tension and horror in her sequence, and it is a shame we really don't see more of her in the film
Her character is more of a symbol rather than a performance as she barely has any speaking lines in this movie, though she does convey her emotions well acting as Odysseus's conscience as Athena
Plays Calypso well by capturing the seductiveness of not wanting Odysseus to leave; has good chemistry with Damon to help show her seduction and entrapment of Odysseus
Really enjoyed his energy on screen as he does a good job helping show the effects the Trojan War had on him; has good chemistry with Holland
Surprisingly has a very big character as he's Odysseus's second in command, and he rises to the occasion having good chemistry with Damon
Plays the servant role well and acts as the voice of reason in his scenes; has good chemistry with the cast as he uplifts the higher billed castmates he works with

cast.comments: On a grand scale everyone in this massive cast is good and Nolan does a good job handling such an epic ensemble, as there are just way too many big-name actors to juggle in this movie; on a microscale the performances take a slight step back and feel a little stiff compared to his other movies; the chemistry in the cast overall is pretty good, though there are some relationships that are stronger than others

story.comments: The concept is Christopher Nolan's take on The Odyssey, staying mostly true to Homer's version while taking creative liberties to make it feel like a Nolan movie; the plot structure is your typical Nolan non-linear structure as the movie starts at the end of the voyage for the A-plot and uses flashbacks to show how we got to this point, and the B-plot taking place in the present time, with both plots converging at the two-hour mark to have a linear climax for the final 50 minutes; the movie is incredibly plot-dense, and while they are able to pace through the movie well in the first hour, the second hour very much drags on with the side-quests they go on (while the book does have many of these side-quests, it very much feels like the middle hour bloats the movie as it drags down the pace); the movie is pretty true to the original story, and I was a huge fan of how they tackled the siren song sequence as that was my favorite story point from the book; the character writing is not as strong as the book or as I would have wanted as it does paint Odysseus and Penelope pretty well, but kinda leaves the rest of the characters feeling like afterthoughts as if he was not focused on fleshing them out

screenplay.comments: The dialogue is a major issue that really holds this movie back as it never feels really sharp because it is either too dumb or too smart in sequences, going back and forth between modern plain English to unnecessarily complex Homoresque dialogue, that it makes the movie not feel stylistically consistent, which very much makes me believe that Nolan prioritized the movie on a grand macroscale with the world and story-building that he left the screenplay and dialogue as an afterthought; the humor is decent as Nolan incorporates minor quips that he always does in his movies; the symbolism is very similar to the book, though it does harp on more of an anti-war and anti-conquering sentiment where Odysseus feels the guilt for the raping and pillaging his men have been doing after Troy, with the character of Athena representing his guilt, and the main symbol of this movie being about the guilt of a previous generation paving the way for the new generation to change the world they created feels very much like a modern sentiment that Nolan wanted to hammer on; the foreshadowing is pretty strong as the way the story is structured non-linearly, you have to have good foreshadowing to help move the story forward, and the movie also uses many tropes and elements from the book to help create the foreshadowing

score.comments: Complements the movie very well by helping build tension and tone, with well-written themes that serve their purpose; the score is not overarching like Oppenheimer, Interstellar, or The Mandalorian as its focus is more about complementing sequences and not overshadowing the film

cinematography.comments: Hoyte van Hoytema uses the 70mm IMAX format perfectly to build this massive, crystal-clear world, filling up the frame and making the voyage and odyssey feel incredibly immersive; this is a movie that must be watched on the biggest screen possible

editing.comments: Very similar to Nolan's other movies, where it stitches parts of a scene seamlessly to make this movie feel like it is made by a true auteur; uses his typical seamless transitions between flashbacks, fast-forwards, and the present to illustrate how both the past and future drive the present story forward

sound.comments: Great in the action sequences and feels deafening at moments, creating the clashes and clangs of ancient Greek war; however, the dialogue mixing is poor as half of Anne Hathaway's dialogue is inaudible, showing that Nolan still has not figured out dialogue mixing because of his refusal to use ADR, making it obvious the audio was recorded during IMAX shooting.

visual_effects.comments: CGI is very minimal but present; the movie relies heavily on practical effects and movie magic (like forced perspective in the Cyclops sequence) which is admirable but can make some moments look a little goofy, where using CGI instead of being so adamant about practical effects might have looked better; still, many of the action sequences are well designed and the world is built well using a combination of practical and visual effects

production_design.comments: Incredible production design that built the Odyssey from scratch with a handcrafted love letter approach using practical sets that transport you to Ancient Greece, staying true to what older epics were doing.

makeup.comments: Very good as it helps paint these characters, working alongside the costumes to create practical movie magic that brings characters and creatures from Ancient Greece to life

costumes.comments: So what if they are not historically accurate, they paint these characters perfectly and make it just a cool-looking movie, with the Greek armor and robes truly transporting you to an Ancient Greece filled with aura

review.pacing: Pacing is all over the place; the first hour moves incredibly fast to get through a lot of plot, but you don't really notice it because it feels like you go through 2 hours of content in one; the middle hour drags heavily with a lot of side quests where they could have easily cut 15 to 20 minutes; the final 50 minutes redeems the pacing issues from the middle act as it is the right pacing that sets up the climax very well
review.climax: Climax is well-made and ties the story together well, leading into what feels like the right ending, helping show the symbolism of the journey and the realization of the guilt that has been haunting Odysseus since the battle of Troy
review.tone: Tonally it is very much a Christopher Nolan epic that feels stylistically like a companion piece to Interstellar in a Greek mythological setting, exploring very similar themes, messages, and objectives
review.final_notes: Saw early screening in Standard IMAX
review.overall: Overall, The Odyssey is Christopher Nolan on a grand, Homeric epic scale, managing to take a massive book and adapt it into an entertaining under-3-hour movie with well-made practical sets, incredible fight choreography, and amazing world-building that transports you to Ancient Greece; however, the daunting task of adapting such a massive story requires making shortcuts and cramming in a lot of plot, leading to a script that falters with clunky dialogue and a middle hour that really drags with endless side quests; even though the second act takes a step back, the excellent first and third acts truly save the movie, making this a fitting Greek mythological companion piece to Interstellar where Nolan ultimately sticks the landing and does justice to adapting The Odyssey despite its structural issues
